\chapter{Supported Forms, Then Head and Na at Distance}
\label{ch:pa-form-head-debt}
\hlchaptermodality{28}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can rebuild two old supported form shapes and separately retrieve head, its horn history, and the na shape at long distance.}

The learner retrieves head and its inherited horn connection, then recognizes the already-taught na shape without claiming independent writing evidence.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[supported two-line and three-line form]{Two supported lines, then three, at R3}

\label{lesson:PA-R28-form-supported-r3}



\begin{quote}
Keep these old banks visible:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\pa{ਭਾਸ਼ਾ}:} \pa{ਪੰਜਾਬੀ} · \pa{ਹਿੰਦੀ}
\end{quote}

>

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\pa{ਰਿਹਾਇਸ਼}:} \pa{ਪਿੰਡ} · \pa{ਸ਼ਹਿਰ}
\end{quote}

>

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\pa{ਕੰਮ}:} \pa{ਖੇਤੀ} · \pa{ਨੌਕਰੀ}
\end{quote}

Point to \textbf{\pa{ਪੰਜਾਬੀ}}, \textbf{\pa{ਸ਼ਹਿਰ}}, and \textbf{\pa{ਖੇਤੀ}}. Nothing here is new.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn — two supported lines}
Copy only the two requested lines. Check the labels before adding anything.

\subsection*{Your turn — add the third supported line}
Check selection, spelling, and placement one pass at a time.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The models and answers stayed visible, so this is supported guided-copy practice. It does not award independent Punjabi writing evidence.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Head and na return separately at R4}

\label{lesson:PA-R28-head-na-r4}



\begin{quote}
Say the Punjabi word for \textbf{head} from memory. Then read \textbf{\pa{ਸਿਰ}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn — meaning and history}
Keep the two claims together: \textbf{sir} means head, and \textbf{horn} is its surprising English cousin. No new etymology follows.

\subsection*{Your turn — recognize na}
Read \textbf{\pa{ਨ}} once and say \textbf{na}. Do not copy it in this lesson.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \textbf{sir — head — horn}, then point to \textbf{\pa{ਨ}}. This lesson measures listening, speech, and recognition. It does not award independent Gurmukhi writing evidence.
\end{tcolorbox}
